title: explorer-verify envelope
description: The JSON document that toEnvelope() returns and that the CLI prints on stdout with --json (R-AX-5). ok is true exactly when the exit code is 0. Within schemaVersion 1, a release may add fields, error codes and backends, and changes nothing else, so readers ignore fields they do not know and treat an unknown error code by its retryable value and the exit code. Keys appear in the order the properties below list them.

oneOf.description: failed: the explorer rejected the submission. Exit code 1.
A dry run: toEnvelope() of the result of dryRun(), which the CLI prints for verify --dry-run. Nothing was submitted. Exit code 0.

Several backends: toEnvelope() of the result of verifyEach(), which the CLI prints for verify with --backend repeated. ok is true and the exit code 0 only when every outcome is ok. Otherwise the exit code is the first of 6, 4, 3, 2, 5, 1 and 130 that any outcome has, each outcome's code being that of its result or error. A non-zero code names only the first outcome with that code: read result.outcomes for every backend.
An error from the catalogue. The exit code depends on error.code.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this envelope format. A change that removes or changes a field raises it.

backend.description: The backend that answered. A later release may add a backend. Known values in this release: etherscan-v2, etherscan-compatible, blockscout, sourcify, routescan.

success.description: A VerifyResult whose status is verified or already-verified.

explorerUrl.description: The public page of the contract. Absent when the library knows none.

failure.description: A VerifyResult whose status is failed.

reason.description: Why the explorer rejected the submission, with API keys removed.

dryRun.description: A DryRunResult: where verify would go and what the explorer holds now. Nothing was submitted.

apiHost.description: The API host verify would send to, such as sourcify.dev, with the port when it is not the scheme's default.

lookup.description: exact or partial: the explorer holds a match, so verify would not submit. none: it holds none, so verify would submit. skipped: the backend needs an API key and none is set, so no request was sent.

explorerUrl.description: The public page of the contract, for a match. Absent when the library knows none.

each.description: A VerifyEachResult: one outcome per backend, in the order the call listed them.

outcome.description: What one backend of a verifyEach() call ended with. Keys appear in the order backend, ok, then result or error.

oneOf.description: failed: the explorer rejected the submission.
The call on this backend threw. A not-confirmed error carries the handle that resumes this backend alone.

error.description: ExplorerVerifyError.toJSON(): the error without its cause, stack or details.

code.description: The stable error code. Each has its own page, docs/user/reference/errors/<code>.md. A later release may add a code; treat an unknown one by retryable and the exit code. Known values in this release: invalid-input, not-confirmed, unsupported-chain, network, rate-limited, timeout, unexpected-response, in-progress, unknown-state, job-not-found, cancelled, incomplete-input, insufficient-artifact, unsupported-compiler, verification-inconclusive, source-mismatch, missing-api-key, api-key-rejected, quota-exceeded, internal-error, no-metadata-hash, metadata-unavailable, constructor-args-unavailable, proxy-link-pending, proxy-link-unknown-state.

docsUrl.description: The code's own page in the error reference.

retryable.description: Whether trying again may succeed without changing the input. For not-confirmed, try checkStatus with the handle, not a new verify.

handle.description: The handle in its one-line form, ev1:<backend>:<chainId>:<address>:<jobId>, when the error carries one.

handles.description: cancelled only, for a run on several backends: each backend that accepted a submission and had not ended before the cancel, with its handle. Resume each one with checkStatus or explorer-verify status.
